grammarFocus: 间接问句；名词性从句；比较、原因和假设表达综合。
title: The Library Noise Experiment
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章和问题均为模拟教学材料，不是官方雅思试题。请仔细阅读文章，注意间接问句、名词性从句以及比较、原因和假设的表达。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配（通过单选形式）和判断正误/未提及。填空答案必须与原文完全一致，且不超过字数限制。所有解析为中文，证据为原文引用。
passage:
Last month, a small public library in the town of Millbrook decided to test a simple idea: would allowing quiet conversation improve the library experience? The library had always been a silent place, but some visitors said they felt lonely there. The head librarian, Sarah Chen, designed an experiment. She wanted to know whether a little background noise could make people stay longer and feel more comfortable.

For two weeks, the library was divided into two areas. Area A remained completely silent, as before. Area B allowed soft talking, but no phone calls or loud music. Sarah asked visitors which area they preferred and how long they stayed. She also recorded how many books were borrowed from each area. The results were surprising. People in Area B stayed on average 25 minutes longer than those in Area A. However, the number of books borrowed from Area A was slightly higher. Sarah concluded that quiet conversation might encourage people to stay, but silence might help them focus on choosing books.

One visitor, a university student named Tom, said he liked Area B because he could discuss his reading with a friend. "I didn't expect that I would enjoy talking in a library," he said. "But it feels more human." Another visitor, an elderly woman, disagreed. She told Sarah that she came to the library for peace and quiet. "If I want to chat, I go to a café," she explained. Sarah realized that different people have different needs.

Sarah then wondered what would happen if the library offered both options permanently. She thought that maybe the library could have a "quiet zone" and a "conversation zone." She asked herself whether the noise level in the conversation zone could be controlled. She decided to test a third area, Area C, where people could talk but only in whispers. After another week, she found that Area C was the most popular. Visitors said they liked the balance: they could whisper to a friend without disturbing others. The number of books borrowed from Area C was the highest of all three areas.

Sarah's experiment shows that small changes can have big effects. She believes that libraries should adapt to what their users want. "We don't have to choose between silence and noise," she says. "We can offer choices." The library now has three zones, and Sarah plans to continue the experiment for another month. She is curious to know whether the popularity of Area C will last.

To understand why Area C worked so well, Sarah interviewed 30 visitors during the third week. She asked them what they liked most about the whisper zone. Most people said that they enjoyed the feeling of being together with others while still being able to concentrate. One man, a retired teacher, told her that he used to avoid the library because it felt too strict. "Now I can say a quick hello to a friend without feeling guilty," he said. A young mother explained that she could read while her child whispered questions to her. Sarah also noticed that the whisper zone was busiest in the late afternoon, when students came after school. She wondered whether the time of day affected how people used the space. To find out, she compared the number of visitors in Area C at different times. She found that the zone was almost empty in the early morning but very busy between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. This suggested that the whisper zone was especially useful for young people and families. Sarah also asked whether visitors would be willing to pay a small fee to use the whisper zone. Most said no, because they believed the library should be free for everyone. Sarah agreed. She decided that the whisper zone would always be free. She also thought about whether other libraries could copy her idea. She concluded that the experiment was a success, but she knew that every library is different. What works in Millbrook might not work elsewhere. For now, she is happy that her small experiment has made the library a friendlier place.

questions.prompt: What did Sarah Chen want to find out with her experiment?
options: Whether a little background noise could make people stay longer and feel more comfortable.
Whether people preferred to read books or use computers.
Whether the library needed more books.
Whether visitors wanted longer opening hours.
answers: Whether a little background noise could make people stay longer and feel more comfortable.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段明确提到Sarah想知道一点背景噪音是否能让人们停留更久、感觉更舒适。
questions.evidence: She wanted to know whether a little background noise could make people stay longer and feel more comfortable.

questions.prompt: In Area B, what was NOT allowed?
options: Soft talking.
Phone calls or loud music.
Reading books.
Discussing with a friend.
questions.explanation: 第二段提到Area B允许轻声交谈，但不允许打电话或大声放音乐。
questions.evidence: Area B allowed soft talking, but no phone calls or loud music.

questions.prompt: How much longer did people in Area B stay compared to Area A?
options: 10 minutes longer.
25 minutes longer.
40 minutes longer.
They stayed the same amount of time.
questions.explanation: 第二段指出Area B的人平均比Area A的人多待25分钟。
questions.evidence: People in Area B stayed on average 25 minutes longer than those in Area A.

questions.prompt: Which area had the highest number of books borrowed? (Answer with one word: A, B, or C)
questions.explanation: 第四段提到Area C的借书数量是三个区域中最高的。
questions.evidence: The number of books borrowed from Area C was the highest of all three areas.

questions.prompt: What did Tom say about talking in the library?
options: He expected to enjoy it.
He didn't expect that he would enjoy talking in a library.
He thought it was too noisy.
He preferred to study alone.
answers: He didn't expect that he would enjoy talking in a library.
questions.explanation: 第三段中Tom说他没想到自己会喜欢在图书馆里说话。
questions.evidence: "I didn't expect that I would enjoy talking in a library," he said.

questions.prompt: Why did the elderly woman disagree with Tom?
options: She wanted to chat with friends.
She came to the library for peace and quiet.
She thought the library was too small.
She preferred Area B.
answers: She came to the library for peace and quiet.
questions.explanation: 第三段中一位老妇人说她来图书馆是为了安静。
questions.evidence: She told Sarah that she came to the library for peace and quiet.

questions.prompt: What was special about Area C?
options: People could talk loudly.
People could only whisper.
People could not talk at all.
People could make phone calls.
questions.explanation: 第四段提到Area C允许人们说话，但只能低声耳语。
questions.evidence: She decided to test a third area, Area C, where people could talk but only in whispers.

questions.prompt: Which area was the most popular according to the text?
options: Area A.
Area B.
Area C.
All areas were equally popular.
questions.explanation: 第四段说Area C是最受欢迎的。
questions.evidence: After another week, she found that Area C was the most popular.

questions.prompt: What does Sarah plan to do next?
options: Close the library.
Continue the experiment for another month.
Remove all zones.
Build a new library.
answers: Continue the experiment for another month.
questions.explanation: 最后一段提到Sarah计划再继续实验一个月。
questions.evidence: Sarah plans to continue the experiment for another month.

questions.prompt: True, False, or Not Given: The library had more visitors in Area B than in Area A.
options: True
False
Not Given
questions.explanation: 文章提到了停留时间和借书数量，但没有提到哪个区域的访客人数更多。因此是Not Given。
questions.evidence: 文章没有提供关于Area A和Area B访客数量的信息。

grammar.title: 间接问句、名词性从句与比较、原因、假设表达
grammar.explanation: 英语中，间接问句用陈述语序，如 'She wanted to know whether...'。名词性从句可作主语、宾语等，如 'what would happen'。比较表达如 'longer than'，原因表达如 'because'，假设表达常用 'if' 条件句。这些结构能使表达更丰富、准确。
grammar.example: She wanted to know whether a little background noise could make people stay longer and feel more comfortable.

options: She asked me where was the library.
She asked me where the library was.
She asked me where is the library.
She asked me where the library is.
answers: She asked me where the library was.
questions.explanation: 间接问句用陈述语序，且时态需与主句一致。

options: What he said was very important.
What did he say was very important.
What he said it was very important.
What was he said very important.
answers: What he said was very important.
questions.explanation: 名词性从句作主语时用陈述语序。

options: If I will have more time, I would read more.
If I had more time, I would read more.
If I have more time, I would read more.
If I had more time, I will read more.
answers: If I had more time, I would read more.
questions.explanation: 假设条件句表示与现在事实相反，if从句用过去式，主句用would+动词原形。

options: The library is more quieter than the café.
The library is quieter than the café.
The library is more quiet than the café.
The library is quietest than the café.
answers: The library is quieter than the café.
questions.explanation: 比较级中，quiet的比较级是quieter，不需要more。
